ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Two right circular cones with vertices facing down as shown in the figure below contain the same amount of liquid. The radii of the tops of the liquid surfaces are $3 \text{ cm}$ and $6 \text{ cm}$. Into each cone is dropped a spherical marble of radius $1 \text{ cm}$, which sinks to the bottom and is completely submerged without spilling any liquid. What is the ratio of the rise of the liquid level in the narrow cone to the rise of the liquid level in the wide cone?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows two right circular cones with their vertices pointing downward. Each cone contains gray liquid filling the lower conical portion. In the left, narrower cone, the radius of the liquid surface is labeled 3 cm. In the right, wider cone, the radius of the liquid surface is labeled 6 cm. Both cones have vertical dashed center lines, and the liquid surfaces are horizontal ellipses. Reasoning: Let the initial liquid heights measured upward from the vertex be h_n for the narrow cone and h_w for the wide cone. The two cones contain the same volume of liquid. Since the liquid in each cone forms a smaller cone, its volume is V = (1/3)πr^2h. Thus (1/3)π(3)^2h_n = (1/3)π(6)^2h_w. So 9h_n = 36h_w, giving h_n = 4h_w. Each dropped marble has radius 1 cm, so each displaces the same volume, 4π/3. Since both marbles are completely submerged and no liquid spills, the final volume below the liquid surface increases by the same amount in each cone. In a fixed cone, similar cross-sections mean the volume below a liquid level scales as the cube of the height from the vertex. Therefore the same fractional volume increase produces the same height scale factor in both cones: H_n/h_n = H_w/h_w. Hence the rises are proportional to the original heights: Δh_n : Δh_w = h_n : h_w = 4 : 1.

Let the initial liquid heights measured from the vertex be h_n and h_w. From the text, the initial liquid volumes are equal, so using cone volume V=(1/3)πr^2h gives (1/3)π(3)^2h_n=(1/3)π(6)^2h_w, hence h_n=4h_w. Dropping the same radius-1 marble into each adds the same displaced volume, 4π/3, and because both marbles are completely submerged with no spill, the final occupied volumes are also equal. In a fixed cone, similar cross-sections imply volume below a level scales as the cube of the height from the vertex, so the same fractional volume increase gives the same height scale factor in both cones: H_n/h_n=H_w/h_w. Therefore the rises are Δh_n=(k-1)h_n and Δh_w=(k-1)h_w, so Δh_n:Δh_w=h_n:h_w=4:1.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the liquid regions are cones whose vertices are at the bottom tips, with initial surface radii 3 cm in the narrow cone and 6 cm in the wide cone. Let their initial heights be a and b. Equal initial liquid volume gives 9a=36b, so a=4b. Model each cone by a linear radius-height relation r=mh. Thus the narrow cone has slope m_n=3/a and the wide cone has slope m_w=6/b. Since a=4b, m_n=(3/4b)=m_w/8. If the rises are x and y, the added volume caused by the marble is the volume of the frustum from height a to a+x in the narrow cone and from b to b+y in the wide cone: ΔV_n=∫_a^{a+x}π(m_n t)^2dt and ΔV_w=∫_b^{b+y}π(m_w t)^2dt. These two added volumes are equal because the same sphere is submerged in each. Substitute a=4b and m_n=m_w/8. Then choosing x=4y makes the narrow integral transform exactly into the wide integral by t=4u, so the equal-volume condition is satisfied; by monotonicity of volume with rise, this ratio is unique. Hence x:y=4:1.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中有两个开口向上的右圆锥容器，顶点都朝下。左边容器较窄，灰色阴影表示液体，液面是一个圆，图中从轴线到液面边缘标出半径为 3 cm。右边容器较宽，同样有灰色液体区域，液面半径标为 6 cm。两幅图都用虚线表示圆锥的中心轴，液体区域从下方顶点到水平液面形成一个圆锥。

再推理：设左边窄圆锥中初始液体高度为 a，右边宽圆锥中初始液体高度为 b。两者液体体积相同，而圆锥体积为 V=(1/3)πr^2h，所以有
(1/3)π·3^2·a=(1/3)π·6^2·b。
因此 9a=36b，得到 a=4b。

因为每个容器中半径随高度线性变化，设半径 r=mh。窄圆锥在高度 a 处半径为 3，所以 m_n=3/a。宽圆锥在高度 b 处半径为 6，所以 m_w=6/b。由 a=4b，得到
m_n=3/(4b)。
而 m_w/8=(6/b)/8=3/(4b)，所以 m_n=m_w/8。

设窄圆锥液面上升 x，宽圆锥液面上升 y。两个半径 1 cm 的球形弹珠完全浸没，排开相同体积的液体，所以液面上升对应增加的体积相等。窄圆锥增加体积为
ΔV_n=∫_a^{a+x} π(m_n t)^2 dt，
宽圆锥增加体积为
ΔV_w=∫_b^{b+y} π(m_w t)^2 dt。

代入 a=4b 和 m_n=m_w/8。若令 x=4y，则窄圆锥积分区间为从 4b 到 4b+4y=4(b+y)。令 t=4u，则 u 从 b 到 b+y，且 dt=4du。于是
∫_{4b}^{4(b+y)} π((m_w/8)t)^2 dt
=∫_b^{b+y} π((m_w/8)·4u)^2·4du
=∫_b^{b+y} π(m_w u)^2 du，
这正好等于宽圆锥的增加体积。由于液面上升越多，增加体积严格越大，所以该比例唯一。因此 x:y=4:1。

Image description: The figure shows two right circular cones with their vertices pointing downward. Each cone contains gray liquid filling the lower conical portion. In the left, narrower cone, the radius of the liquid surface is labeled 3 cm. In the right, wider cone, the radius of the liquid surface is labeled 6 cm. Both cones have vertical dashed center lines, and the liquid surfaces are horizontal ellipses.

Reasoning: Let the initial liquid heights measured upward from the vertex be h_n for the narrow cone and h_w for the wide cone. The two cones contain the same volume of liquid. Since the liquid in each cone forms a smaller cone, its volume is V = (1/3)πr^2h. Thus
(1/3)π(3)^2h_n = (1/3)π(6)^2h_w.
So 9h_n = 36h_w, giving h_n = 4h_w.

Each dropped marble has radius 1 cm, so each displaces the same volume, 4π/3. Since both marbles are completely submerged and no liquid spills, the final volume below the liquid surface increases by the same amount in each cone. In a fixed cone, similar cross-sections mean the volume below a liquid level scales as the cube of the height from the vertex. Therefore the same fractional volume increase produces the same height scale factor in both cones: H_n/h_n = H_w/h_w. Hence the rises are proportional to the original heights:
Δh_n : Δh_w = h_n : h_w = 4 : 1.
